name: Root & Rally
title: Root & Rally | Supplements, Herbs and Teas for Everyday Immune Support
description: Plain-language guides to supplements, herbs and teas that support your immune system day to day and help you rest up when you're run down. Every pick shows its evidence level and cautions.

hero.title: Everyday support for your immune system.
hero.text: Simple guides to what people take to stay well, and to rest up when they're run down. Every pick shows what the research says and who should be careful.

notice.title: Talk to your doctor first,
notice.text: especially if you take medications, are pregnant or nursing, or have a health condition. Supplements can interact with medicines.

evidence.title: How to read the evidence levels

strong.label: Strong
strong.text: Reviews of multiple good-quality human trials agree there is a benefit.

some.label: Some
some.text: Human trials exist, but they are small, mixed or low-certainty.

limited.label: Traditional use
limited.text: A long history of use or early lab research, with little human trial data.

doctorBox.title: When to see a doctor
doctorBox.text: Supplements are not a substitute for medical care. Call your doctor if you have any of these.
items: A fever of 103°F (39.4°C) or higher, or any fever lasting more than 3 days
Symptoms that last more than 10 days, or get worse after starting to improve
Trouble keeping fluids down, very little urine, or dizziness when standing
A severe sore throat, earache, sinus pain or headache
Any fever in a baby under 3 months old
You are pregnant, over 65, or have a chronic condition and feel very unwell
doctorBox.emergency: Call 911 right away for trouble breathing, chest pain, confusion, fainting, or bluish lips or face.

sourcesPage.title: Sources
sourcesPage.description: The studies and references behind every evidence level on Root & Rally.
paragraphs: Every evidence level on this site comes from published research. We lean on systematic reviews first (Cochrane and peer-reviewed meta-analyses), then U.S. National Institutes of Health fact sheets (the Office of Dietary Supplements and NCCIH), then individual trials.
Research changes. If you spot something out of date, let us know and we will review it.
